```{r call_libraries_and_functions, echo=FALSE, cache=FALSE}
# obtained from https://www.r-bloggers.com/how-to-draw-venn-pie-agram-multi-layer-pie-chart-in-r/ 
# inputs numbers for different categories:
## data input (number of reads mapped to each category)
total=100
rRNA=5 # mapped to nuclear rRNA regions
mtRNA=7  # mapped to mitochondria genome
# for the rest of above, then we divide into different category, like http://www.biomedcentral.com/1741-7007/8/149 did.
intergenic=48 
introns=12
exons=30
upstream=3
downstream=6
not_near_genes=40

# modifications: 
# 1) no central pie, all are doughnuts so the central bit can be for the total count and 'main'
# 2) add counts to all legend categories displayed
vennPie_modified <- function() {

  rest=total-rRNA-mtRNA
  genic=rest-intergenic
  introns_and_exons=introns+exons-genic
  
  # parameters for pie chart
  iniR=0.2 # initial radius
  colors=list(NO='white',total='black',mtRNA='#e5f5e0',rRNA='#a1d99b',genic='#3182bd',intergenic='#fec44f',introns='#fc9272',exons='#9ecae1',upstream='#ffeda0',downstream='#fee0d2',not_near_genes='#d95f0e')
  
  library('plotrix')
  
  # from outer circle to inner circle
  #0 circle: blank
  pie(1, radius=iniR, init.angle=90, col=c('white'), border = NA, labels='')
  
  #4 circle: show genic:exons and intergenic:downstream
  floating.pie(0,0,c(exons, genic-exons+not_near_genes, downstream, mtRNA+rRNA+intergenic-not_near_genes-downstream),radius=5*iniR, startpos=pi/2, col=as.character(colors[c('exons','NO','downstream','NO')]),border=NA)
  
  #3 circle: show genic:introns and intergenic:not_near_genes | upstream
  floating.pie(0,0,c(genic-introns, introns, not_near_genes, intergenic-upstream-not_near_genes, upstream, mtRNA+rRNA),radius=4*iniR, startpos=pi/2, col=as.character(colors[c('NO','introns','not_near_genes','NO','upstream','NO')]),border=NA)
  
  #2 circle: divide the rest into genic and intergenic
  floating.pie(0,0,c(genic, intergenic, mtRNA+rRNA),radius=3*iniR, startpos=pi/2, col=as.character(colors[c('genic','intergenic','NO')]),border=NA)
  
  #1 circle: for rRNA+mtRNA+rest
  floating.pie(0,0, c(rest, rRNA,mtRNA), radius=2*iniR, startpos=pi/2, col=as.character(colors[c('NO','rRNA','mtRNA')]), border = NA)
  
  legend(0, 5*iniR, gsub("_"," ",names(colors)[-1]), col=as.character(colors[-1]), pch=19,bty='n', ncol=2)
  
  ## or, in one column with reads count and %
  #names=gsub("_"," ",names(colors)[-1])
  #values = sapply(names(colors)[-1], get)
  #percent=format(100*values/total, digits=2, trim=T)
  #values = format(values, big.mark=",", scientific=FALSE, trim=T)
  #cl=as.character(colors[-1])
  #pchs=rep(19, length(cl)); pchs[1]=1;
  #legend(0, 5*iniR, paste(names," (",values,", ", percent,"%)", sep=""), col=cl, pch=pchs,bty='n', ncol=1, cex=0.6)
} 

# same columns in input (snps) and output table
# previously made sure all columns have multiple entries, and same number in each column, for each row
split_one_line_per_SNP <- function(snps, sep=";", 
                                   columns=c("CHR_ID", "CHR_POS", "STRONGEST.SNP.RISK.ALLELE", 
                                             "SNPS", "CONTEXT")) {
  # initiate an empty data.frame
  snps_extended <- data.frame(matrix(nrow=0, ncol=ncol(snps)), stringsAsFactors=F)
  colnames(snps_extended) <- colnames(snps)
  
  for (k in 1:nrow(snps)) {
  #snps_extended <- apply(snps, 1, function(x) {
    x <- snps[k,]
    
    # that's how many SNPs are in this line
    n <- length(unlist(str_split(x[,columns[1]], sep))) 
    df <- data.frame(matrix(nrow=n, ncol=0), stringsAsFactors=F)
    
    for(i in 1:ncol(snps)) {
      # needs splitting
      if (colnames(snps)[i] %in% columns) {
        splt <- unlist(str_split(x[,colnames(snps)[i]], sep))
        df <- cbind(df, splt)
      }
      # just copy over
      else {
          df <- cbind(df, rep(x[,colnames(snps)[i]], n))
      }
    }
    colnames(df) <- colnames(snps) # df is now expanded to n rows, each with one SNP
    snps_extended <- rbind(snps_extended, df)
  }
  return(snps_extended)
}

# will add LDblock range
# inputs a GRanges with all SNPs; a dir with .tsv files with LDs within 1MB centred on each SNP, 
# and the threshold to include SNP pair
# outputs the same gr, with additional LDblock metadata column spanning the range of all DNPs with LD above threshold
# (will return NA if the 1MB file is missing or empty)
add_LDblock <- function(gr, LDdir, LDcutoff=0.6) {

  gr$LDblock <- ""

  for (i in 1:length(gr)) { 
    
    # reconstruct 1Mb range around
    r <- granges(trim(promoters(gr[i], upstream=500000, downstream=500000)))
    start(r) <- start(r)-1
    
    # find the right LDfile
    strng <- paste0(seqnames(r), "_", start(r), "_", end(r), ".tsv")
    LDf <-  list.files(LDdir, pattern=strng)
    print(paste0("[", i, "/", length(gr), "] ", LDf))
    
    # checking that the non-empty file exists
    if(length(LDf)>0 & file.info(paste0(LDdir, LDf))$size>0) {
      
      df <- read.table(paste0(LDdir, LDf), quote="", stringsAsFactors=F)
      
      # first SNP is our GWAS SNP, and second has >=0.6 LD with it
      infirst <- which(df[,2]==start(gr[i]) & df[,5]>=LDcutoff)
      
      # second SNP is our GWAS SNP, and first has >=0.6 LD with it
      insecond <- which(df[,4]==start(gr[i]) & df[,5]>=LDcutoff)
      
      all_snps <- c(start(gr[i]),
                    df[insecond,2],
                    df[infirst,4])
      
      gr$LDblock[i] <- paste0(seqnames(gr[i]), ":", 
                                       min(all_snps), "-", 
                                       max(all_snps)) # span of all SNPs in 0.6 LD with gr[i]
    }else{
      gr$LDblock[i] <- NA
    }
  }
  return(gr)
}

# if an LD block spans two GRbs, we will merge these together
# if we are wrong, this will simply inflate the number of E-P pairs and drop the p.adj due to correcting for more tests but should not be too detrimental
# input is the GRanges of GRBs and which parameter, i.e. a list of pairs/multiples to be merged
# score becomes the mean of the scores for GRBs to be merged
merge_grbs_overlapping_same_locus <- function(grbs, w) {
  toremove <- numeric()
  toadd <- GRanges()
  
  for(i in 1:length(w)) {
    newGr <- GRanges(seqnames=seqnames(grbs[w[[i]]][1]),
                     ranges=IRanges(start=min(start(grbs[w[[i]]])), 
                                    end=max(end(grbs[w[[i]]]))))
    newGr$name <- paste0("merged:", 
                         paste0(as.character(grbs[w[[i]]]), collapse=";"))
    newGr$score <- mean(grbs[w[[i]]]$score)
    newGr$itemRgb <- grbs[w[[i]][1]]$itemRgb # don't care about this one at this point
    newGr$thick <- IRanges(start=start(newGr)+1, end=end(newGr))
    newGr$targets <- paste(grbs[w[[i]]]$targets, collapse=",")
    
    toadd <- c(toadd, newGr)
    toremove <- c(toremove, w[[i]])
  }
  grbs <- grbs[-toremove]
  grbs <- sort(c(grbs, toadd))
  return(grbs)
}
```

## GWAS detected SNPs
We are loading SNP data from `r input_snps_csv` table. Variant data were downloaded from GWAS catalog on 2016-12-02. This table needs quite a bit of work to be usable. 

```{r load_GWAS_SNPs_data_into_GRanges, echo=F, cache=T}
# read in SNP csv -> will require these post-processing steps:
# 0) set aside interaction SNPs and figure out whether to include them or not
# 1) removing odd lines where one position is reported, but multiple SNPs
# 2) splitting the csv into rows that have one SNP per line (fine), and the multiSNP lines (need fixing)
# 3) split multiSNP lines into inividual SNP ones and append these to the fine ones
# 4) remove non-rs lines and SNPs with no position
# [5)] infer LD blocks (consider staring with only European ones)
# ancestry is not always 1+1 thus a separate sheet - use for  LD block inference
# [6)] remap to hg19
# [7)] add positions to SNPs that map to hg19 and not hg38
# will need remapping to hg19 positions, also check the ones with lacking coordinates whether these map to hg19
csv <- read.csv(input_snps_csv, stringsAsFactors=F, sep="\t")
```

```{r SNPxSNP_interactions, echo=F, cache=T}
# 0) set aside interaction SNPs and figure out whether to include them or not
i <- sort(unique(c(grep("x", csv$CHR_ID), grep("x", csv$CHR_POS)))) # pos where 2 SNPs in interactions
f <- "GWAScatalog_interacting_csv.rds"
saveRDS(csv[i,], f)
csv <- csv[-i,]
```

The `r length(i)` positions with several SNPs interacting in each position have been eliminated from further analysis and saved for future use in `r f`.

#### Splitting multiSNP lines
First problem are lines that refer to multiple SNPs (all falling within the same haplotype). First we remove the lines where multiple SNPs are present, but fewer positions or SNP contexts are present in the same line.

```{r inconsistent_multiSNP_removal, echo=F, cache=T}
# 1) removing odd lines where one position is reported, but multiple SNPs
# the lines that can have ";" separated multiple values, one per SNP
columns2consider <- c("CHR_ID", "CHR_POS", 
                      "STRONGEST.SNP.RISK.ALLELE", "SNPS", "CONTEXT")
multiSNP_lines <- sapply(columns2consider, function(x) {
  grep(";", csv[,x])
})
multiSNP_lines <- unique(unlist(multiSNP_lines))
uniqSNP_lines <- 1:nrow(csv)
uniqSNP_lines <- uniqSNP_lines[!(uniqSNP_lines %in% multiSNP_lines)]

# determine the rows of csv where there isn't the same number of entries in these 5 multi-columns
df <- data.frame(matrix(nrow=length(multiSNP_lines), ncol=length(columns2consider)))
  
for(i in seq_along(columns2consider)) {
  df[,i] <- sapply(csv[multiSNP_lines, columns2consider[i]], function(x) {
    length(unlist(str_split(x, ";")))
  })
}

w <- apply(df, 1, function(x) { length(unique(x)) })
how_many <- length(which(w>1))
multiSNP_lines <- multiSNP_lines[w<2] # only keeps the lines where all 5 columns have same number of entries -> eliminated 5 lines (*)
```

There were `r how_many` lines like that, and we removed them. Next, all multiSNP lines need to be split (splitting columns `r columns2consider`) into one line per SNP.

```{r multiSNP_splitting, echo=F, cache=T}
# 2) splitting the csv into rows that have one SNP per line (fine), and the multiSNP lines (need fixing)
# csv[uniqSNP_lines] are fine, csv[multiSNP_lines] are to be split one SNP per line (barring 5 dodgy ones in *)
# 3) split multiSNP lines into inividual SNP ones and append these to the fine ones
snps_extended <- split_one_line_per_SNP(snps=csv[multiSNP_lines,], sep=";",
                                        columns=c("CHR_ID", "CHR_POS", "STRONGEST.SNP.RISK.ALLELE", 
                                                  "SNPS", "CONTEXT"))
new_csv <- rbind(csv[uniqSNP_lines,], snps_extended)
```

```{r remove_nonSNP and make_GRanges, echo=F, cache=T}
# 4) remove non-rs lines and lines with no SNP position
before <- nrow(new_csv)
new_csv <- new_csv[grepl("rs", new_csv$SNPS),]
```

Next step is removing `r before-middle` variants that lacked 'rs' in their SNP name, i.e. indels, HLA, 'kgp' and 'chr11:107967350'-like IDs. Then all lines where there is no `CHR_POS` or `CHR_ID` are removed (`r middle-after` of them). N.B. these used to exist in chrN:num and chrN_num formats - glorious.

For the moment, we'll subset only the variants in studies that were tested on European population: these are the most ubiquitous and easiest to ascertain LD blocks, since these have not been automatically provided.


```{r extract_European_studies, echo=F, cache=T}
# [5)] infer LD blocks (consider staring with only European ones)
input_ancestry_csv <- "../GWAScatalog_2016-12-02_allAncestry.tsv"
ancestry_cols <- scan(input_ancestry_csv, what=character(), sep="\t", nlines=1)
ancestry <- read.delim(input_ancestry_csv, stringsAsFactors=F, row.names=NULL)
ancestry[,ncol(ancestry)] <- NULL
colnames(ancestry) <- ancestry_cols

u <- unique(ancestry$`STUDY ACCCESSION`)

# for each study, accept only if initial study was done on European population
studiesInitialEUR <- character()
for(i in seq_along(u)) {
  lns <- ancestry[ancestry$`STUDY ACCCESSION`==u[i],]
  lns <- lns[lns$STAGE=="initial"] # only initial have to be Eur
  if(all(lns$`BROAD ANCESTRAL CATEGORY`=="European")) {
    studiesInitialEUR <- append(studiesInitialEUR, u[i])
  }
}
  
# for each study, accept only if all phases (initial and replications) were done on European population
studiesAllEUR <- character()
for(i in seq_along(u)) {
  lns <- ancestry[ancestry$`STUDY ACCCESSION`==u[i],]
  if(all(lns$`BROAD ANCESTRAL CATEGORY`=="European")) { # all have to be Eur
    studiesAllEUR <- append(studiesAllEUR, u[i])
  }
}

saveRDS(studiesAllEUR, paste0(study_name, "_studiesAllEUR.rds"))
```

Out of `r length(u)` GWAS studies included in this edition of the Catalog, in `r length(studiesInitialEUR)` the initial study was done on an European population, and in `r length(studiesAllEUR)` studies all stages were done on European population. In this first instance only the variants in studies fully conducted on the European population will be interrogated, as it is quite straightforward to obtain the linkage disequilibrium information for these.


There were `r length(bed.gr)` SNPs both detected and validated in the EUR population as significant. A 1Mb region with the SNP in the center is created for each of these SNPs, and ranges are saved in `./1MB_around_SNPs_files/` (1 file per chr), to be used for LD calculation.

Arbitrarily, SNPs within this 1Mb region (half a megabase each side) around the GWAS SNP, and with LD of 0.6 or greater within EUR population are kept, comprising the `GWAS locus` of that SNP.

## GRBs
We are using human:mouse (hg19:mm10) GRBs here. Therefore our SNPs need to be lifted over to hg19 before we can detect the ones overlapping human:mouse GRBs.

Question 3: Should we focus on the more distant pairwise species' comparison, or a range of GRBs?


```{r lifting_over_to_h19, echo=F, cache=T}
# [6)] remap to hg19
# making file of coordinates to liftOver
ch <- import.chain("../../hg38ToHg19.over.chain")
#new_csv$SNP.position.hg19 

#new_SNPs.EUR.hg19.gr <- unlist(liftOver(new_SNPs.EUR.gr, chain=ch))
new_SNPs.EUR.gr$hg19.coords <- ""
new_SNPs.EUR.gr$LDblock.hg19 <- ""

for(i in 1:length(new_SNPs.EUR.gr)) {
  print(i)
  hg19.coor <- unlist(liftOver(new_SNPs.EUR.gr[i], chain=ch))
  if(length(hg19.coor)>1) {
    print(paste0("two mappings for ", as.character(new_SNPs.EUR.gr[i])))
  }else if (length(hg19.coor)==1){
    new_SNPs.EUR.gr$hg19.coords[i] <- as.character(hg19.coor)
    
    # now the same for the LD block
    gr <- unlist(liftOver(GRanges(new_SNPs.EUR.gr$LDblock[i]), chain=ch))
    gr <- reduce(gr, min.gapwidth=50)
    gr <- subsetByOverlaps(gr, GRanges(new_SNPs.EUR.gr$hg19.coords[i]))
    
    if(length(gr)>1) {
      print(paste(i, new_SNPs.EUR.gr[i]$SNPS, 
                  as.character(new_SNPs.EUR.gr[i]), 
                  as.character(gr), sep=" "))
    }else if (length(gr)==1){
      new_SNPs.EUR.gr$LDblock.hg19[i] <- as.character(gr)
    }
  }
}
#this is utterly slow, rewrite!

new_SNPs.EUR.hg19.gr  <- GRanges(new_SNPs.EUR.gr$hg19.coords)
mcols(new_SNPs.EUR.hg19.gr) <- subset(mcols(new_SNPs.EUR.gr), , 
                                      -c(LDblock, hg19.coords))
saveRDS(new_SNPs.EUR.hg19.gr, "new_SNPs.EUR.hg19.gr.rds")
```

Now let's create a GRanges with LD (loci) information:

TO DO: add some stats on these LD blocks (total genomic coverage, avg size, percentage overlapping, number of LDs with size 1 - no SNPs in LD)...

```{r make_loci_object, cache=F, echo=F}
loci.hg19.gr <- unique(GRanges(new_SNPs.EUR.hg19.gr$LDblock.hg19)) # we cannot merge overlapping ones different traits and LDs!

# collect gene info from $REPORTED.GENE.S. and $MAPPED_GENE fields
loci.hg19.gr$gwas_genes <- ""
loci.hg19.gr$SNP.position <- ""
loci.hg19.gr$SNPs <- ""
loci.hg19.gr$trait <- ""

# consider not merging at all, leaving all from orig. SNPs as ind. lines
for(i in 1:length(loci.hg19.gr)) {
  w <- which(new_SNPs.EUR.hg19.gr$LDblock.hg19==as.character(loci.hg19.gr[i]))
  genes <- c(unlist(str_split(new_SNPs.EUR.hg19.gr$REPORTED.GENE.S.[w], ", ")), 
             unlist(str_split(new_SNPs.EUR.hg19.gr$MAPPED_GENE[w], " - ")))
  # mapped gene can also have semicolon-separated genes
  genes <- unlist(str_split(genes, "; "))
  genes <- unique(genes[!is.na(genes)])
  genes <- genes[!genes %in% c("intergenic")]
  
  loci.hg19.gr$gwas_genes[i] <- paste(genes, collapse=",")
  loci.hg19.gr$SNP.position[i] <- paste(new_SNPs.EUR.hg19.gr$SNP.position[w], collapse=",")
  loci.hg19.gr$SNPs[i] <- paste(new_SNPs.EUR.hg19.gr$SNPS[w], collapse=",")
  loci.hg19.gr$trait[i] <- paste(new_SNPs.EUR.hg19.gr$MAPPED_TRAIT[w], collapse=";")
}
saveRDS(loci.hg19.gr, file=paste0(study_name, "_loci.hg19.gr.rds"))
```

## SNPs in GRBs summary
Same categories as above, make Venn diagrams

```{r GRB_overlap, cache=F, echo=F}
loci_in_GRBs.gr <- subsetByOverlaps(loci.hg19.gr, grbs)
ovlp <- findOverlaps(loci_in_GRBs.gr, grbs)
  
# merging GRBs that are overlapped by the same LD block
q <- queryHits(ovlp)[duplicated(queryHits(ovlp))] #loci overlapping two GRBs
# each element list is a set of GRBs to merge as these overlap the same locus
w <- lapply(q, function(q) {
  return(subjectHits(ovlp)[queryHits(ovlp)==q])
})
grbs <- merge_grbs_overlapping_same_locus(grbs, w)
ovlp <- findOverlaps(loci_in_GRBs.gr, grbs)

# adding GRB coordinates to each locus
loci_in_GRBs.gr$grb.coords[queryHits(ovlp)] <- as.character(grbs[subjectHits(ovlp)])
  
snps_in_GRBs.gr <- subsetByOverlaps(new_SNPs.EUR.hg19.gr, loci_in_GRBs.gr)
saveRDS(snps_in_GRBs.gr, paste0(study_name, "snps_in_GRBs.gr.rds"))
```

```{r SNP_in_GRBs_summaries, echo=F, cache=F, eval=F}
# to do: now SNPs are in hg19, adjust....
t <- loadDb("hg10.ensGene.txdb") #needs to be loaded again!
# first, annotate with hg19 ensGene annotation
snpInGRBsAnno <- annotatePeak(peak=snps_in_GRBs.gr, tssRegion=c(-3000, 3000),
                             TxDb=t, annoDb="org.Hs.eg.db",
                             genomicAnnotationPriority = c("5UTR", "3UTR", "Exon", "Promoter",
                                                           "Intron", "Downstream", "Intergenic"))
# add annotation of CAGE-based TSSs for every transcript in a gene
plotAnnoPie(snpInGRBsAnno)
vennpie(snpInGRBsAnno)

# SNP count of ones in exons
exon_count <- round(sum(snpInGRBsAnno@annoStat$Frequency[grep("exon", snpInGRBsAnno@annoStat$Feature, ignore.case=T)]) * length(snps_in_GRBs.gr) / 100)
nonexon_genic_count <- round(sum(snpInGRBsAnno@annoStat$Frequency[grep("intron|utr", snpInGRBsAnno@annoStat$Feature, ignore.case=T)]) * length(snps_in_GRBs.gr) / 100)
intergenic_count <- round(sum(snpInGRBsAnno@annoStat$Frequency[grep("intergenic", snpInGRBsAnno@annoStat$Feature, ignore.case=T)]) * length(snps_in_GRBs.gr) / 100)
```

There are `r length(loci_in_GRBs.gr)` loci (each with one SNP) overlapping human:mouse GRBs. `r exon_count` is coding, `r nonexon_genic_count` are intronic and UTR, and`r intergenic_count` are distal intergenic.

```{r make_all_loci_summary_object, echo=F, cache=T}
# makes sure to work on the GRB level, even when one GRB covers multiple loci
grb_subset <- subsetByOverlaps(grbs, loci_in_GRBs.gr)
saveRDS(grb_subset, paste0(study_name, "_grb_subset_GeThesisTargets.rds"))
loci.gr <- loci_in_GRBs.gr

byGRB_list <- vector("list", length(grb_subset))
names(byGRB_list) <- str_replace_all(as.character(grb_subset), "[:-]", "_")

loaded_chr <- "" # for second and third element

for (i in 1:length(grb_subset)) {
  
  # make each element a list of length 3
  byGRB_list[[i]] <- vector("list", 4)
  print(paste0("Processing ", names(byGRB_list)[[i]], " GRB [", i, "/", length(grb_subset), "]"))
  
  # fill in the first element - df of gene classification for that GRB
  byGRB_list[[i]][[1]] <- per_GRB_genes_classification(grb_subset[i], loci_in_GRBs.gr)
  
  if(!identical(loaded_chr, as.character(seqnames(grb_subset[i])))) {
    
    loaded_chr <- as.character(seqnames(grb_subset[i]))
    rho_gr <- load_per_chr_rho_file(loaded_chr)
    empP_gr <- load_per_chr_empP_file(loaded_chr)
    
  }
  
  # fill in the second element - df of spearman's rho
  byGRB_list[[i]][[2]] <- per_GRB_correlation_matrix(rho_gr, grb_subset[i], byGRB_list[[i]][[1]]$ens)
  
  # fill in the third element - df of mutual information scores
  #byGRB_list[[i]][[3]] <- per_GRB_mi_matrix(mi_gr, grb_subset[i], byGRB_list[[i]][[1]]$ens)
  
  # fill in the fourth element with empP of seeing enhancer expression and high promoter expression for the same samples
  byGRB_list[[i]][[3]] <- per_GRB_empP_matrix(empP_gr, grb_subset[i], byGRB_list[[i]][[1]]$ens)
    
  # fill in the fourth element with information on enhancers in this GRB
  byGRB_list[[i]][[4]] <- per_GRB_enhancers_classification(fantom5.enhancers.tpm.gr, grb_subset[i], 
                                                           byGRB_list[[i]][[1]]$ens, 
                                                           loci.hg19.gr, TSSs.perTranscript.gr)
}

saveRDS(byGRB_list, paste0(study_name, "_byGRB_list_wEnhancers_GeThesisTargets_pooledFANTOM5.rds"))
```
